author: The Fortune Teller
title: Beware! 3 Indicators You Mustn't Ignore
text:
Don't get me wrong: We're still bullish!... Bullish but careful... Investing but more defensively... Trapping Value but protecting the (Wheel of) FORTUNE ...
Here's why...
Yield Curve: Beware! The yield curve has proved itself over the years to be an important - and a very reliable - way to predict whether a recession is approaching. As things stand right now, the yield curve signaling that the US economy is getting closer to a recession.
The most popular (yield-curve-related) indicator investors look at is the spread between the 2 and 10-year US treasury yields (as it's now"10-2" hereinafter)
10-2 Year Treasury Yield Spread data by YCharts Over the past decade, the 10-2 hasn't been that close to turn negative as it's now.
Sure, there are many indicators that support the strong economy and/or bullish market thesis; we are not trying to challenge those. However, the 10-2 is an indicator that proved itself over a very long period and, therefore, it mustn't be taken lightly.
As a matter of fact, an inverted yield curve has proven itself historically (to be a reliable indicator for an upcoming recession) in the last 9 out of 10 times !
90% accuracy rate isn't something you wish to ignore or underestimate.
Tech Stocks: Beware! We all know the FAAMG-(American)-gang: Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Google-Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ).
We also know the BAT-(Chinese)-man: Baidu ( BIDU ), Alibaba ( BABA ), and Tencent ( OTCPK:TCEHY ).
These eight stocks represent not only the world's hottest tech companies but also the world's two largest economies: US ( SPY , QQQ ) and China ( FXI , MCHI ).
This collective of stocks is commonly being referred to as FAAMG+BAT or (my own preferred version) the gang-man ...
Here are few facts about the FAAMG+BAT gang-man :
There are only 5 "SELL" on FAAMG stocks out of 199 analyst ratings. There are no "SELL" recommendations on Apple ( AAPL ) or Google-Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) at all. It now has a total worth of no less than $5 trillion! AAPL Market Cap data by YCharts If this number doesn't impress you (enough), allow me to say that $5T is more than what the entire stock market of three other large economies is worth.
The total market cap of the Eurozone stock market is "only" $4.9T The total market cap of EM (excluding the BAT trio) stock markets is "only" $4.5T The total market cap of the Japanese stock market is "only" $3.6T So $5T is a really big - and significant - number.
According to BoAML's ( BAC ) global fund-manager survey, being long " the gang-man " is (and has been) the most crowded trade in the market over the past year. It's no wonder then to see BoAML's chief investment strategist, Michael Hartnett, suggesting that (investors might be too optimistic about future earnings of " the gang-man " and, as a result) this "oversize" is a good reason for investors to reduce their exposure to tech stocks .
As a side note, it's important to note that this significant size is only one out of 10 reasons that Michael Hartnett is providing for cashing out of tech stocks .
Full disclosure: We are still investing in tech stocks
(Large-Cap) Growth/Value Ratio: Beware! Large-caps growth to value ratios are at 17-year high!

Beware! Allow me to finish by quoting from Howard Marks of Oaktree Capital most recent memo to clients:
It's not hard to imagine the popularity that fueled the growth of ETFs in good times working to their disadvantage in bad times.
You can easily replace the word "ETFs" with "tech stocks", "growth stocks", "FAAMG+BAT" or simply with "stocks"...
